Opinion polling was carried out prior to the [[2018 Mexican general election]].

The 2018 Mexican election features nine registered political parties, including the [[Institutional Revolutionary Party]] (PRI), [[National Action Party (Mexico)|National Action Party]] (PAN), [[Party of the Democratic Revolution]] (PRD), and the newly formed [[National Regeneration Movement]] (Morena).

==Coalition backgrounds==
===Todos por México===
PRI, which held the presidency from 1929 to 2000 and is currently in power under President Peña Nieto, is primarily a [[Centre-right politics|center-right]] party. It will be contesting the elections in a coalition alongside the [[Ecological Green Party of Mexico]] and the [[New Alliance Party (Mexico)]] under the coalition "''[[Todos por México]]''" ("Everyone for Mexico").

===Por México al Frente===
PAN is a center-right, [[Christian democracy]]<ref>{{cite book |first=Soledad |last=Loaeza |author-link=Soledad Loaeza |title=The National Action Party (PAN): From the Fringes of the Political System to the Heart of Change |work=Christian Democracy in Latin America: Electoral Competition and Regime Conflicts |publisher=Stanford University Press |year=2003 |page=196 |isbn=9780804745987 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ppe20kevrzgC&pg=PA196}}</ref> party which held the presidency in 2 [[Sexenio (Mexico)|sexenios]] from 2000-2012.

PRD grew out of the PRI in 1986 as the leftists who created the ''Corriente Democrática'' ([[National Democratic Front (Mexico)|Democratic Current]]) within PRI split off. It came quite close to claiming the presidency in [[2006 Mexican general election|2006]]. Surprisingly, the PRD decided to form a coalition with the right-wing PAN, and they will contest the elections alongside [[Citizens' Movement (Mexico)|Citizens' Movement]] in a coalition called "''[[Por México al Frente]]''" ("For Mexico, to the Front").<ref name=":1">{{cite web|title=PAN, PRD y MC avalan Frente pero sin definir sus alcances|url=https://politico.mx/central-electoral/elecciones-2018/pan-avala-frente-opositor-con-el-prd-para-2018/ |access-date=September 5, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diariocambio.com.mx/2017/nacional/item/19923-se-confirma-el-frente-opositor-pan-mc-y-prd-iran-en-alianza-para-2018|title=Se confirma el Frente Opositor: PAN, MC y PRD irán en alianza para 2018|access-date=September 5, 2017|website=DiarioCambio.com.mx|language=es-es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=El PAN, el PRD y Movimiento Ciudadano constituirán un frente común para 2018|url=http://expansion.mx/politica/2017/09/04/el-pan-el-prd-y-movimiento-ciudadano-constituiran-un-frente-comun-para-2018|access-date=September 5, 2017|work=Expansión|language=es-MX}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite news |title=Registran Frente Amplio ante el INE|url=http://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/politica/registran-frente-amplio-ante-el-ine|date=September 5, 2017|access-date=September 5, 2017|work=El Universal|language=es}}</ref>

===Juntos Haremos Historia===
MORENA, created in 2014 by [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]], affectionately called AMLO, is a left-leaning party which split from the PRD.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mexicoinstituteonelections2015.wordpress.com/the-parties/|title=The Parties|date=2014-09-17|work=The Mexico Institute's 2015 Elections Guide |access-date=2017-04-19 |df=mdy-all |language=en}}</ref> It will contest the elections as a coalition with the [[Labor Party (Mexico)|Labor Party]] (PT) and the [[Social Encounter Party]] (PES), called "''[[Juntos Haremos Historia]]''" ("Together we'll make history").
